obligation: Banking organization notification incident (bank)
trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, the bank's ability to serve a material portion of its customers, a business line whose failure would cause a material loss, or operations whose failure would threaten U.S. financial stability
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident has occurred
notify: OCC supervisory office or OCC-designated point of contact (email or telephone)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - national bank (53.1(c)). Determine and record the decision with date and time for every severity 1 and 2 incident (POL-03 4.4); reassess when facts change
clock_starts: Determination time recorded by the incident commander and CISO

obligation: Banking organization notification incident (parent)
trigger: Notification incident that affects Cris Santos Company, Inc., the bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the parent determines a notification incident has occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - U.S. bank holding company (225.300(c)); decided at the same time as the OCC determination because the bank is about 98% of the parent

obligation: Bank service provider notice to the bank (inbound)
trigger: Provider determines an incident has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, covered services to the bank for four or more hours (not scheduled maintenance)
deadline: As soon as possible after the provider's determination
notify: Bank-designated point of contact (Cyber Defense Center shared mailbox and phone); if none was given, the CEO and CIO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty of bank service providers (treasury platform vendor, card processor, core software vendor, others). Contacts still missing for 9 critical providers (POAM-019)

obligation: Regulator notice of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B, Supplement A II.A.1.b (guidance)
trigger: Bank becomes aware of an incident involving unauthorized access to or use of sensitive customer information (for example, a client's treasury user name and password, or a name with an account number or Social Security number)
deadline: As soon as possible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - interpretive guidance examined as part of the response program; separate from the 53.3 notice

obligation: Customer notice under the response program
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B, Supplement A III.A to III.C (guidance)
trigger: Reasonable investigation shows misuse of the customer's information has occurred or is reasonably possible
deadline: As soon as possible; delay only if law enforcement determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation and asks in writing
notify: Affected customers (clear and conspicuous notice with the Supplement A III.B content)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Chief Privacy Officer decides and documents; in the BEC scenario the affected commercial clients and the individuals whose data was in the mailbox

obligation: Suspicious activity report
trigger: Known or suspected federal criminal violation: any amount for insider abuse; $5,000 or more with an identifiable suspect; $25,000 or more regardless of a suspect
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection; up to 30 more days to identify a suspect, never more than 60 days after initial detection
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BSA/AML Officer; every fraudulent wire of $25,000 or more requires a SAR
clock_starts: Initial detection of facts that may be a basis for filing

obligation: Immediate notice of an ongoing violation
trigger: A reportable violation that needs immediate attention, such as an ongoing fraud
deadline: Immediately, by telephone, in addition to the timely SAR
notify: Appropriate law enforcement authority and the OCC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the attacker is still active (more fraudulent requests or live sessions)
clock_starts: When the ongoing violation is identified

obligation: Board notice of SAR filing
trigger: A SAR is filed
deadline: Promptly after filing
notify: Board or the committee it designates (audit committee)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: SAR confidentiality
trigger: Any communication during the incident
deadline: Throughout; never disclose a SAR or information that would reveal one
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies to client, media, and investor communications (POL-05 4.10)

obligation: Report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center
trigger: Fraudulent wire from business email compromise
deadline: As soon as possible after discovery; fast reporting improves the chance of freezing funds
notify: FBI through ic3.gov; FBI field office for large losses
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but required by the runbook; supports the SAR and any law enforcement delay request

obligation: Wire recall request to the beneficiary bank
citation: Payment system practice; funds transfer agreement (contract)
trigger: A wire the bank sent is suspected to be fraudulent
deadline: Immediately on discovery, before the beneficiary bank releases funds
notify: Beneficiary bank wire or fraud desk (phone, then written request); Federal Reserve payment services message where available
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the most time-critical step; not a legal notice

obligation: Refund of an unauthorized payment order (Florida worked example)
citation: UCC Article 4A as enacted in the governing state; Florida: Fla. Stat. 670.202 and 670.204
trigger: A payment order accepted in the client's name is not authorized and not effective as the client's order, for example because the bank did not follow the agreed security procedure
deadline: Refund with interest from the date the bank received payment; counsel determines effectiveness under 670.202
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - governing law is set in the treasury agreement (Florida for most clients). Counsel decides; whether the agreed security procedure was followed is central

obligation: SEC materiality determination
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Release 33-11216); 17 CFR 229.106(a) (a series of related unauthorized occurrences is one cybersecurity incident)
trigger: Any cybersecurity incident, including related occurrences, that may be material to a reasonable investor
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
notify: Disclosure committee (internal decision, recorded with date and time)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - parent is an Exchange Act reporting company. Related BEC occurrences must be assessed together (POAM-017)
clock_starts: Discovery (the determination starts the filing clock)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: The disclosure committee determines an incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after the materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material or reasonably likely material impact; no technical details that would impede response

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay only for the period the Attorney General specifies
notify: Department of Justice (request through outside counsel)
applies_at_this_tier: Only in that case; not expected in a BEC incident

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe the incident's effect, if material, and any process changes (for example, the move of the cyber risk oversight team)

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Workforce with knowledge of a potential material cybersecurity incident
deadline: Immediately when the disclosure committee convenes
notify: Committee members, responders, and executives with knowledge
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy

obligation: SEC Reg S-P customer notification (broker-dealer)
trigger: Unauthorized access to or use of sensitive customer information of the broker-dealer's customers is reasonably likely, and no determination that substantial harm or inconvenience is not reasonably likely
deadline: As soon as practicable, not later than 30 days after becoming aware; delay only on an Attorney General determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if broker-dealer customer information is involved (for example, if the compromised mailbox held brokerage client records). Not triggered in the worked example

obligation: SEC Reg S-P service provider notice to the broker-dealer (inbound)
trigger: A service provider becomes aware of a breach resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system it maintains
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 72 hours after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound; 14 of 31 contracts still lack the term (POAM-021)

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example, "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; outside counsel's state matrix

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set threshold of affected residents
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where a state requires it

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where a state requires it

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information of a Florida individual (includes name with Social Security number, a financial account number with a required access code or password, or a user name with a password that permits access to an online account)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (up to 15 more days on written good cause); notice under the primary federal regulator's rules is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Supplement A customer notice meets the deemed-compliance path if a copy goes to the Department
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: Only at 500 or more Floridians; not triggered in the worked example (260 Floridians)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only above 1,000; not triggered in the worked example

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (worked example)
trigger: Bank decides notice is not required because, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the bank relies on the no-harm exception; not expected when Social Security numbers were exposed

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the bank (worked example, inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent that maintains data for the bank has a breach
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound; 5 inherited contracts silent on the duty (POAM-019)

obligation: Commercial client notice under the treasury management agreement
trigger: Client credentials, accounts, or payments affected
deadline: Per agreement (same business day for suspected unauthorized payments)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Financial institution bond and cyber insurance notice
trigger: Loss or suspected loss from fraud or a security incident
deadline: Per policy; notify the carrier before hiring response vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not in a BEC incident; kept for extortion scenarios (POL-03 4.8)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then)

obligation: FDIC and NCUA incident notification
trigger: Notification incident at an FDIC-supervised bank; reportable incident at a credit union
deadline: 36 hours (FDIC); 72 hours (NCUA)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the OCC is the bank's primary federal regulator (Part 53 applies instead); no credit union

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers at an institution under FTC jurisdiction
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank is OCC-supervised; the broker-dealer is SEC-regulated

obligation: NYDFS cybersecurity incident and extortion payment
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a NYDFS-regulated entity; extortion payment
deadline: 72 hours after determination; 24 hours after payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - no group entity holds a NYDFS license, registration, or charter

obligation: Insurance licensee cybersecurity event
citation: NAIC Model #668 sec. 6 (as adopted by states)
trigger: Cybersecurity event at an insurance licensee
deadline: 72 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - no insurance licensee in the group

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the group holds federal contracts with these clauses; none identified for this incident type
